[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] DartPoints own site describes a strategy of delivering enterprise grade colocation, cloud, and managed infrastructure services to communities outside the largest United States metros, operating in Tier 2 and Tier 3 regional markets. The company began operations in the early 2000s. DartPoints is headquartered at 1601 Elm Street, Suite 3650, Dallas, Texas. This session refreshed and sharpened a prior research passes brief note that the company received a strategic growth investment from NOVA Infrastructure in 2025: per both DartPoints own press release and independent trade press corroboration from Data Center Dynamics, both fetched fresh this session, NOVA Infrastructure actually acquired majority control of DartPoints, announced April 30, 2025, with lending partner Orion Infrastructure Capital, committing more than 250 million dollars in combined growth capital, while the prior owner, Astra Capital Management, retained a meaningful minority stake. As part of that same transaction, DartPoints acquired the underlying real estate for three of its data centers, in Greenville, South Carolina, Baton Rouge, Louisiana, and Asheville, North Carolina, per both sources. DartPoints own site lists 11 facilities across 10 markets, including Baton Rouge, Louisiana (2 facilities) and Shreveport, Louisiana, Cincinnati and Dublin, Ohio, Columbus, Indiana, Asheville, North Carolina, and Columbia, Greenville, Charleston, and Spartanburg, South Carolina, matching every state where this registry lists a DartPoints facility, and DCD independently corroborates the same 11 facility, 10 market count and adds that the company serves more than 900 enterprise customers including Fortune 500 companies, universities, and hospital systems. The company emphasizes AI ready, high density infrastructure, 99.999 percent uptime, and SOC 2 Type II compliance. This specific row, the Shreveport, Louisiana facility (internal code SHV01), per the operators own dedicated location page for this facility, fetched fresh this session, sits at 601 Milam St, Shreveport, LA 71101, in downtown Shreveport per the embedded location context on that page.

reading.body:
DartPoints Shreveport in Shreveport, Louisiana, publishes 2.2 MW of IT capacity, operated by DartPoints.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 220 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 55 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

No compliance certifications are published for DartPoints Shreveport. That does not mean none exist, only that this site's dataset, built from the operator's own facility page, does not list any, which limits what regulated workloads a reader could confirm the facility is qualified to host.

Louisiana has 3 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 3 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 7.7 MW. DartPoints Shreveport contributes 2.2 MW of that total. At that published size it is a small facility relative to what frontier AI training infrastructure requires, which now runs into the tens or hundreds of megawatts, though it may still support inference workloads or smaller-scale AI applications.
